When packaged with PingDirectory, the Admin Console is running on Jetty, this violates the exploitability criteria of running on Tomcat. When shipped as a standalone Admin Console, the customer should not run the .war file on a Tomcat server. Regarding the docker image that runs Admin Console, this is being shipped with Tomcat out of the box, and could be vulnerable to CVE-2022-22965. We are prioritizing an emergency fix for this. We recommend that customers lock down access to their Admin Console until a new image is released, if the attacker can not access it via HTTP requests they will not be able to exploit it. The PingDirectory CLI can be leveraged if configuration changes need to be made while the admin console is down.

This finding is a false positive as PingDirectory does not use the commons-text methods which implement StringLookup as described in https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-42889. PingDirectory uses the simple StringSubstitutor.replace() and TextStringBuilder.appendln() methods only, not the potentially vulnerable createInterpolator() method. None of the replace() or appendln() overrides contain StringLookup, StringLookupFactory or createInterpolator.

See https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-text/apidocs/src-html/org/apache/commons/text/StringSubstitutor.html  & https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-text/apidocs/src-html/org/apache/commons/text/TextStringBuilder.html.

PingDirectory only uses Kafka as a client and not as a vulnerable server as described in this CVE. The Synchronization Server has the ability to use Kafka as a sync destination, but in that regard it operates only as a client that can send messages to a Kafka server that a customer manages. To ensure non-exploitability for customers that use Apache Kafka Server, we are upgrading Apache Kafka Connect to fixed version 3.4.0. If a customer uses Kafka Connect in their environment, we advise them to validate connector configurations and only allow trusted JNDI configurations until the next PingDirectory release.

Not affected. CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Node.js built-in Brotli decoder, exploitable only where a Node.js runtime decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. PingDirectory does not ship or execute a Node.js runtime: the Node.js-built UI is compiled ahead of time into static JavaScript bundles served by the product, and at request time the browser (not Node.js) renders it and performs any Content-Encoding decompression using the browser's own Brotli implementation, which is separate code and not affected by this CVE. Node.js is used only in CI build containers, which are not deployed to production.
